methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, functionalities, and constraints. Each atomic unit represents a distinct and independent piece of information necessary for understanding and implementing the 100-bit left/right rotator. The goal was to create units that are technically specific, unambiguous, and directly implementable. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements, focusing on the 'what' rather than the 'how'.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Rotator shifts-in the shifted-out bit from the other end of the register
Load input loads register with data[99:0]
Load is synchronous and active high
ena = 2'b01 rotates right by one bit
ena = 2'b10 rotates left by one bit
q represents the contents of the rotator
Rotation occurs on the rising edge of the clock signal (clk)
When 'load' is asserted high, the register 'q' is loaded with 'data[99:0]', overriding any rotation
When 'load' is not asserted, the rotation is enabled
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module implements a 100-bit left/right rotator
Rotator has synchronous load
Rotator has left/right enable
Module has input clk
Module has input load
Module has input ena[1:0]
Module has input data[99:0]
Module has output q[99:0]
When load is asserted, q is loaded with data
ena controls rotation direction
ena = 2'b01 rotates q right by one bit
ena = 2'b10 rotates q left by one bit
ena = 2'b00 or ena = 2'b11 results in no rotation
Rotation is implemented using bit concatenation
Right rotation is achieved by concatenating the LSB of q with the remaining bits
Left rotation is achieved by concatenating the MSB of q with the remaining bits
Load operation has priority over the rotation operation
The next state of register q depends on the current values of load, ena, and data at the rising edge of clk
The register updates its value on the rising edge of the clock clk
The updates to q are performed using non-blocking assignments <=.
